column1: # Obligation citations — goal 0009a (freeze the native oracle), the machine-checked half of the
# increment's acceptance surface (docs/goals/0009a-native-oracle.md).
# **What a row here is, exactly.** This increment makes no Go change (its Bounds), so it adds no Go test;
# docs/conventions.md still holds a citations row to be one *gate-runnable Go test* in a package
# scripts/gate-targets.txt covers. Every row below therefore names one **oracle rule** — the rule ids are
# `scripts/codex-native-check.py`'s `ORACLE_RULES` keys — and the existing Go test that already pins the
# same claim about this tree's own bytes: the sentence the rule restates, true of the writer today and
# re-derived by this step when the gate runs. Where the rule states more than one clause, the `artifact`
# cell names the clause the cited test pins, and the row is no claim of conjunct-level coverage of the
# whole sentence. A row makes no claim that a Go test runs the oracle.
# The oracle's own firing is re-derived by the required `selftest` step instead:
# `scripts/tests/test_codex_native_check.py`'s `CodexArtifactOracle` holds the rule table and its mutation
# table in bijection — every rule has at least one committed synthetic fixture whose mutation turns that
# rule red and no other, and a mutation without a rule fails too
# (`test_every_rule_has_a_mutation_that_turns_its_fixture_red`, the increment's D1). The fixtures are
# `scripts/tests/testdata/codex-oracle/` (the two synthetic artifacts, their manifest receipts).
# Deliberately not covered, with the reason (form-based: a row is one Go test in a package
# scripts/gate-targets.txt covers, so a rule whose gate re-derivation is a python case the required
# `selftest` step runs, or a native harness run, cannot hold one):
#   oracle.receipt, oracle.plan-emitted, oracle.plan-accounted, oracle.plan-order, oracle.plan-pairs —
#         the manifest-receipt half. No Go test grounds it, because nothing in this tree produces a
#         receipt yet: the receipt's producer is goal 0009c/0009d (this goal's Non-scope), and the rules
#         are stated over the synthetic receipts committed with the fixtures. Their re-derivation is the
#         same `selftest` case's mutation table (four mutations for `oracle.receipt`, two for
#         `oracle.plan-emitted`, twelve for `oracle.plan-accounted`, two for `oracle.plan-order` and
#         one for `oracle.plan-pairs`), plus `test_a_reduced_artifact_is_validated_from_the_artifact_alone` (D2),
#         `test_a_receipt_that_declares_nothing_cannot_pass` (the plan is total: an empty receipt is
#         refused before comparison, a metadata-only artifact included),
#         `test_a_result_substituted_under_one_call_id_is_refused` (a result's identity is its call and
#         its recorded text), `test_a_call_substituted_under_one_call_id_is_refused` (a call's
#         identity is its call id, name and recorded input),
#         `test_a_custom_calls_recorded_input_is_part_of_its_identity` (a `custom_tool_call`'s recorded
#         input lives in `input`, and the receipt's `arguments` member names it there) and
#         `test_a_written_empty_object_input_is_part_of_the_identity` (the identity is the member the
#         artifact writes — the writer's own `arguments: "{}"` is not the read's empty answer, and a
#         receipt naming one does not certify the other) — the two
#         substitution cases and the recorded input's own written form, beside the mutation table's own
#         pinned refusals. `test_a_boundarys_replacement_history_is_refused_with_a_plan`,
#         `test_receipt_validation_refuses_the_occurrences_it_cannot_name` (a `response_item` a read
#         turns into an occurrence the receipt's vocabulary cannot name — the inter-agent `agent_message`
#         addressed to the session's own agent path among them — is refused where a plan is compared)
#         and
#         `test_a_malformed_member_is_named_without_echoing_its_text` pin three more refusals the mutation
#         table also holds (a boundary's `replacement_history` refused where a plan is compared; an
#         unnameable occurrence refused; a
#         string `call_id` named by digest and never echoed). Review round r5's refusals are pinned by
#         `test_a_line_with_a_duplicate_member_is_refused` (a line whose object writes a member name
#         twice — and a receipt whose object does — is refused before comparison; its rule is the
#         `oracle.jsonl-objects` row above, and it carries its own mutation in the `selftest` table), by
#         the object-valued-`content` arms of
#         `test_receipt_validation_refuses_the_occurrences_it_cannot_name` and by
#         `test_a_written_empty_object_input_is_part_of_the_identity`'s both-members arm (a shape whose
#         read this oracle does not model is refused where a plan is compared); the latter two are
#         refusals under `oracle.plan-accounted`, whose executed reverts stand in
#         docs/evidence/0009a-native-oracle.md §10.
#         Review round r6's refusals are pinned by
#         `test_a_developer_role_message_is_refused_with_a_plan` and
#         `test_a_custom_tool_call_output_is_refused_with_a_plan` (a `message` in a role outside the
#         writer's two carrying readable text, and a result in the family whose carried read answers an
#         outcome this route's writer's own results have no member for — each refused where a plan is
#         compared, green without one, and counted among the twelve `oracle.plan-accounted` mutations above)
#         and by `test_a_call_without_a_usable_name_is_no_call` (a call whose `name` is not the
#         non-empty string the carried reader registers is refused with its orphaned output, and no
#         receipt — the fixture's own or one edited to `name: ""` — certifies the pair: the new clause
#         of the `oracle.call-pairing` row above, whose cited Go test pins the rule's other clause),
#         with the executed reverts of all four new mutations in
#         docs/evidence/0009a-native-oracle.md §11.
#         Review round r7's refusals are pinned by
#         `test_a_result_the_receipt_cannot_establish_is_refused_with_a_plan` (a result whose call the
#         read answers elsewhere — `spawn_agent` links a subagent session and appends no result,
#         `wait`/`wait_agent` answer per-agent results from the output's own `status` object, the
#         exec-cell poll excepted — or whose output no read appends a result from is refused where a
#         plan is compared, green without one),
#         `test_a_non_string_identity_member_is_refused_with_a_plan` (a call's recorded input or a
#         result's recorded text written as a non-string member is refused where a plan is compared,
#         its JSON spelling — which reconstructs the receipt's own string key — pinned as the identity
#         it would otherwise be matched on, and the explicit-`null` identity `null` distinguished from
#         the absent member's empty string) and
#         `test_a_moved_turn_context_is_outside_the_receipts_vocabulary` (a record's turn placement is
#         outside what the receipt states; the finding's own `turn_context` move validates green), with
#         the four new mutations' executed reverts and the scope pin's inverted study in
#         docs/evidence/0009a-native-oracle.md §12.
#   the oracle's `--validate` mode — the CLI half of the same python subject
#         (`test_the_validate_mode_reports_a_verdict`, and
#         `test_decoded_input_never_aborts_validation`: a decoded string strict UTF-8 cannot encode and a
#         string member nested past Python's parser each end in the documented verdict and exit code
#         rather than a traceback); no native-or-Go half exists for it.
#   D1 — every rule has its own negative fixture: the `selftest` case named above.
#   D2 — the oracle needs no knowledge of the source or the selection: the same case's
#         `test_a_reduced_artifact_is_validated_from_the_artifact_alone` drives the validator with
#         `builtins.open`, `io.open` and `os.open` (the names `pathlib`'s reads resolve among them)
#         refusing every file — and shows each refusal fires — and §2 of
#         docs/evidence/0009a-native-oracle.md validates the reduced fixture from a scratch directory
#         that holds nothing else.
#   D3 — the existing acceptance path is unchanged: `scripts/codex-native-check.py`'s own unflagged run is
#         a native harness run, not a gate step; its before/after verdicts are quoted in §3 of the record
#         (26 check(s) passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped, exit 0, both times) and the acceptance path itself is a
#         Go suite the `test` step already runs.
#   D4 — the freeze is stated where a later lane reads it: prose in the checker's own oracle section,
#         docs/harness.md and AGENTS.md; the oracle-lock signal that enforces it is the conductor's, not a
#         command in this tree.
